Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 64 (NocRoom missing-address campaign): found two conflicting, mutually uncorroborated candidate addresses, a reverse geocode of this rows own coordinates near Miami International Airport and a separate aggregator listing for a downtown Miami facility roughly 12 kilometers away, neither confirmed by this operators own site, and declined to guess which if either applies to this row.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] NocRoom is a Miami, Florida based provider describing colocation, IP transit, network based services, and local IT services (fiber and copper network installation, PBX VOIP, email, IP routing, servers, virtualization) across Los Angeles, Dallas, and Miami on its own site. This specific facility level reading supplements an earlier operator level pass already on file for this operator. This operators own homepage, refetched this session, describes only city level service areas and gives no facility specific street address, and a contact page and an about page both failed to fetch this session due to the sites own robots file returning a server error. Reverse geocoding this rows own independently stored coordinates through a third party geocoding service returned 7415 Northwest 19th Street, near Miami International Airport, as the nearest addressable building to this exact point, though nothing on this operators own site confirms a facility at that address. Separately, a facility specific aggregator listing named a distinct NocRoom facility in downtown Miami at 36 Northeast 2nd Street, roughly 12 kilometers from this rows own coordinates, describing it as an all fiber network serving downtown Miami colocation, dedicated servers, and hosted PBX. Given these two candidate addresses conflict and neither is confirmed by this operators own site as tied specifically to this row, this session declines to apply either as this rows confirmed address.

reading.body:
This facility publishes no power specification, rack count, or IT load figure. NocRoom describes itself as a Miami-based colocation and local IT services provider with presence in three cities, and this specific facility's address remains unconfirmed after research attempts found two conflicting candidate locations near Miami International Airport and downtown Miami, neither verified by the operator's own published site. Without confirmed location or published capacity, this facility cannot be ranked among Florida's disclosed data center power footprint.

Florida has published capacity figures for only four facilities totaling 9.35 MW across the state. This facility, unmeasured, would rank fifth by presumed size if it held any published specification, but contributes nothing to the state's disclosed total. The state has 13 mapped facilities in OpenStreetMap, indicating most colocation providers in Florida publish no power figures at all.

For an AI scaling decision, this facility offers no actionable information. No power capacity is public, no certification or tenant type is stated, and physical location is unconfirmed. Colocation providers that do not publish load figures are not useful signals about AI infrastructure deployment.
